findings.title: Retry-count deletion branch is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch in the deleteMany is only `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) restriction, while `retryCount` is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder table used for EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP reminders. Any non-SMS reminder whose retryCount exceeds 1 will therefore be deleted by this SMS cron job even though it was never attempted here. The branch should be scoped to SMS (and unscheduled) reminders like the first branch.

findings.title: Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without any nested try/catch. If that update fails — e.g. Prisma P2025 because the reminder was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation/reschedule, or a transient DB error (which may be the same error that triggered the catch) — the exception propagates out of the for loop and out of the handler. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are then skipped and the cron returns an error, whereas previously the catch only logged and the loop continued with the next reminder.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message never increment retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only runs inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (either the else branch for a falsy Twilio result or the catch). When `sendTo` is falsy — e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` is null/missing for SMS_ATTENDEE, a permanently invalid case — or when the rendered message is empty, neither branch executes, so retryCount stays 0 and the reminder is re-selected by every cron invocation until its scheduledDate passes. This leaves unfixed the endless-rescheduling loop the PR is meant to stop for missing/invalid numbers.

findings.title: Retry counter uses stale read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both increment sites write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (a run processing many reminders can outlive the cron interval), both read the same value and write the same incremented value, losing a failure count and causing extra scheduling attempts (including possible duplicate Twilio calls). Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.
